title: Docker Launches Fully Rebuilt Virtualization Layer to Boost Performance and Improve Dev Experience
gist: Docker replaced its third-party virtualization component with a first-party 'Docker VMM' engine in Docker Desktop 4.86, claiming faster container startup and lower memory use, and framing the same engine as the shared foundation for both traditional containers and its AI-agent sandbox product.

insights.claim: Docker replaced its long-standing third-party virtual machine monitor with a first-party engine, Docker VMM, built from the ground up and now controlled end-to-end by Docker itself, launched as public beta in Docker Desktop 4.86 for Mac (auto-enabled) and Windows (opt-in).
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Signals Docker vertically integrating a core dependency it previously outsourced, reducing reliance on third-party VMM vendors and giving it control over release cadence and tuning.
insights.quote: Now it runs on Docker VMM, built by us from the ground up. That means we own the full stack, and we can tune every part of the engine for container workloads specifically.
insights.locator: Docker Desktop has always relied on a third-party VMM

insights.claim: Docker claims the new VMM delivers measurably faster container startup across first launch, project switching, and restart recovery, improved file sharing between host and container that particularly benefits edit-compile-test workflows, and better memory efficiency by returning unused memory when containers are idle.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A developer-experience improvement claim worth benchmarking against alternatives like OrbStack, Colima, or Podman Desktop before switching workflows.

insights.claim: On Windows, Docker now owns the virtualization layer directly and is targeting Hyper-V-level isolation while delivering performance closer to WSL2, addressing a historically weaker Windows experience relative to Mac.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Could reduce the incentive for Windows developers to bypass Docker Desktop in favor of WSL2-native container setups.
insights.locator: An additional benefit is better experience on Windows

themes.theme: Unified runtime for containers and AI agents

insights.claim: The same Docker VMM engine also powers Docker Sandboxes, Docker's isolated execution environments for AI agents, with Docker stating its longer-term goal is a unified runtime spanning laptops, cloud, and on-prem where containers, Compose applications, and AI agents share the same foundation.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Positions Docker as infrastructure for agentic AI execution, a potential new product surface competing with dedicated AI-sandbox providers as agent workloads scale.
insights.locator: The same virtualization engine powers Docker Sandboxes

insights.claim: Linux support for the new VMM is deferred to general availability, expected end of October 2026, meaning the current beta covers only Mac and Windows.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A concrete timeline marker for enterprises planning rollout or evaluating adoption risk on Linux-based dev fleets.
insights.locator: Currently, the new VMM is included in Docker Desktop 4.86
